== 1. UPSTREAM'S DECLARED TYPE, and it is one union in FOUR places ==
   ops.py:758  copy_to_device(self, device:str|tuple[str, ...], arg=None)
   ops.py:677  allreduce(self, op, device:str|tuple[str, ...])
   spec.py:140 is_device(d) = isinstance(d,str) or (isinstance(d,tuple) and all strs)
   ops.py:33   ParamArg.device: str|tuple[str, ...]|None = None

== 2. UPSTREAM STORES IT VERBATIM AND THEN BRANCHES ON IT ==
   COPY.arg          = ('CPU', 'CPU')   (tuple)
   ALLREDUCE.arg     = (Ops.ADD, ('CPU', 'CPU'))
   ALLREDUCE.arg[1] == COPY.arg -> True    <- ONE value, so the two
                                                        spellings below cannot BOTH be right
   device_range_src(('CPU','CPU')) -> 1 src
   device_range_src('CPU')         -> 0 src
   valid_device_range(('CPU',), ()) = False   <- a TUPLE of any length needs a DEVICE range src
   valid_device_range('CPU',    ()) = True   <- a STR needs none. Third upstream branch on the union.

== 3. THE FLATTEN WAS NOT INJECTIVE. This is what decided it. ==
   pre-fix  2 devices ('CPU','CPU')        -> sCPU,CPU               post-fix -> n(sCPU,sCPU)
   pre-fix  1 device, as a TUPLE ('CPU',)  -> sCPU                   post-fix -> n(sCPU)
   pre-fix  1 device, as a STR   'CPU'     -> sCPU                   post-fix -> sCPU
   pre-fix  1 device NAMED 'CPU,CPU'       -> sCPU,CPU               post-fix -> n(sCPU,CPU)

   pre-fix  ('CPU',) == 'CPU'        -> True   <- COLLIDES: upstream's isinstance(device, tuple)
   post-fix ('CPU',) == 'CPU'        -> False
   pre-fix  ('CPU,CPU',) == ('CPU','CPU') -> True   <- COLLIDES
   post-fix ('CPU,CPU',) == ('CPU','CPU') -> False

== 4. THE PORT NEVER LACKED THE REPRESENTATION; the TEXT did ==
   LAWS/spec.bend:85  type Dev is Data:  D1{tag: U32} | Dn{tags: List<&2,U32>}
   uop/ops.bend:1070  ADev{dev: S.Dev}     <- the COPY arg, and it holds a PAIR
   uop/ops.bend:1071  AAllred{rop: Op, dev: S.Dev}
   graphcmp.bend      g_allred built O.ADev{S.Dn{[0,0]}} and it COMPILED and PRINTED
                       before ADEV-1. The premise 'a pair has no port representation'
                       was FALSE about the Arg and TRUE only about graphcmp's renderer.

== 5. THE DISARM NULL: a fresh object of the same value is the SAME ucache node ==
   rebuilt is r            -> True
   toposort len clean/armed-> 9 / 9
   and the emitted py stream is byte-identical: md5 90ec1dda91a8d761f293669aa0a5bd6d
   for `--plant devdisarm` AND for no plant, against 2580f38166cb2bfc078b3ffca0f03429
   for `--plant devpair`. (measured with `graphcmp.py emit --side py --graph allred`)

== 6. WHAT py's TWO SPELLINGS WERE, AND WHICH IS WRONG ==
   pre-fix  COPY      -> n(sCPU,sCPU)    (no carg arm for Ops.COPY -> the generic _carg tuple grammar, which NESTS)
   pre-fix  ALLREDUCE -> al(OADD,sCPU,CPU)   (carg arm -> the flattening dev)
   post-fix COPY      -> n(sCPU,sCPU)
   post-fix ALLREDUCE -> al(OADD,n(sCPU,sCPU))
   Both pre-fix spellings are ONE value (`c.arg == r.arg[1]` above) in ONE graph, two
   nodes apart. The GRAPH is not inconsistent -- THE PRINTER WAS. So 'is py's
   inconsistency upstream's or the differ's?' has one answer: THE DIFFER's, and on BOTH
   sides -- bend's flatten double-prefixed to `ssCPU,sCPU`, which is a THIRD spelling of
   the same value and matches neither. Upstream is answerable to neither.
